claim: In its FY2025 10-K (fiscal year ended 31 October 2025), Synopsys describes its business as solutions spanning silicon design, silicon IP, simulation and analysis (S&A) and design services.
evidence: "We deliver trusted and comprehensive solutions spanning silicon design, silicon intellectual property (IP), simulation and analysis (S&A) as well as design services." (Item 1. Business, Company and Segment Overview, FY2025 10-K)
notes: S&A comes from the Ansys merger (10-K: 'With ANSYS, Inc, (Ansys) now part of Synopsys'). The FY2024 wording (EDA + silicon IP) is in CLM-0493.

claim: Synopsys named Cadence Design Systems and Siemens EDA as EDA competitors in its FY2024 10-K, but its FY2025 10-K describes EDA competitors only generically, without naming them.
evidence: FY2024: "Our competitors include EDA vendors that offer varying ranges of products and services, such as Cadence Design Systems, Inc. and Siemens EDA." FY2025: "We compete with a variety of different EDA vendors, including publicly traded companies offering varying ranges of products and services..." (Item 1, Competition)

claim: Through fiscal 2025 (ended 26 October 2025), Applied Materials' Applied Global Services segment also manufactured and sold 200mm and other equipment, a business moving to the Semiconductor Systems segment from the first quarter of fiscal 2026.
evidence: "Through October 26, 2025, our AGS segment also manufactured and sold 200 millimeter (200mm) and other equipment to customers globally that serve non-leading-edge markets. Effective the first quarter of fiscal 2026, our 200mm equipment business will be moved to our Semiconductor Systems segment." (Item 1, Applied Global Services)
notes: Qualifies CLM-0511's description of AGS as purely post-sale: in FY2025 the segment still included some new 200mm equipment sales.

claim: In May 2026 Arm said it expects the first revenue from production sales of its own chip (the Arm AGI CPU) in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027, the quarter ending March 2027.
evidence: CFO Jason Child: "we are maintaining our outlook of $1 billion while we pursue supply chain capacity, and we still expect the first revenues from production shipped sales to land in the fourth quarter of this fiscal year." (Q4 FY2026 call, 6 May 2026, 0:12:11; Arm's fiscal year ends 31 March)
notes: The Yahoo/Quartr transcript renders 'production shipped sales'; Morningstar's transcript snippet reads 'production chip sales'. The Arm IR transcript PDF (SRC-0213) could only be read in excerpts. 'This fiscal year' on 6 May 2026 = FY2027 (Apr 2026-Mar 2027).

claim: In July 2026 Arm said initial Arm AGI CPU product had been delivered to multiple customers and it had secured manufacturing capacity for its US$1 billion AGI CPU opportunity across fiscal 2027 and 2028, with customer demand above US$2 billion.
evidence: "Initial product has been delivered to multiple customers, and we have secured the manufacturing capacity required to support the $1 billion opportunity we outlined last quarter across fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028. Customer demand has accelerated beyond our initial expectations and now exceeds $2 billion across fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028." (Q1 FYE27 shareholder letter)
notes: Newer status for CLM-0501/CLM-0566: Arm has started delivering its own chips, but the letter does not report chip revenue for the quarter.
